column4: Visit note | 2025-05-12 09:30 AM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Mostafa Haque, 34, male. Mr. Haque reports suffering from poor sleep, constant worry for months, and tense muscles that make it difficult for him to relax. He works as a nurse and mentions that these anxious feelings began after witnessing a severe road accident in Mirpur. He feels overwhelmed during his shifts and experiences racing thoughts at night. He denies feeling depressed, suicidal ideation, or palpitations. On examination: GAD-7 score 15, BP 124/85 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, weight 86 kg. He is alert and oriented, though visibly tense. Assessment: Generalized anxiety disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued today to help manage his symptoms. He was advised to practise slow breathing daily, reduce tea and coffee intake, and start regular counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.
